questions.question: Before answering a constructed-response prompt, what should a student do?
choices: Identify what the question asks and the evidence needed
Write immediately without reading the prompt
Copy the longest passage
Guess the expected answer from the page number

questions.question: A multiple-choice question asks for the 'best evidence.' What should the student choose?
choices: The longest quotation
The option that most directly supports the stated claim
A detail on the same topic but unrelated to the claim
The option with the most familiar wording

questions.question: A student is unsure about one question and time is limited. What is a useful strategy?
choices: Spend all remaining time on it
Leave the rest unanswered
Mark it, continue with other questions, and return if time remains
Change answers randomly

questions.question: What should a student do before submitting a written response?
choices: Add unrelated details
Remove all transitions
Check only the title
Check that it answers the prompt and includes clear support

questions.question: A question uses the word 'except.' What should the student notice?
choices: The task is to identify the choice that does not fit
The answer must be the longest
The question is asking for a summary
The choices should be ignored

questions.question: Two answer choices appear plausible. What can help distinguish them?
choices: Choose the first one
Return to the question wording and compare each choice against the evidence
Select the most dramatic choice
Use the same letter as the previous answer

questions.question: A student changes an answer during review. When is the change most justified?
choices: Whenever the answer feels unfamiliar
To make the pattern of letters even
When the student finds evidence or a clear reason that the first choice is wrong
When the question takes a long time

questions.question: Why should a student read every answer choice before selecting one?
choices: The choices are always arranged from wrong to right
The first choice is never correct
Reading all choices guarantees a perfect score
A later option may be more complete or accurate than the first plausible one

questions.question: A test has a graph and a question about a trend. What should the student inspect first?
choices: The axes, labels, units, and relevant data points
The graph's color palette
The page border
The answer choices only

questions.question: What is a reasonable use of elimination?
choices: Remove choices only because they are short
Remove choices that conflict with the prompt or evidence
Eliminate the correct answer to make the task easier
Choose randomly among all options

questions.question: A student finishes early. What is the most useful review?
choices: Change every answer once
Submit without review
Recheck unanswered items, directions, calculations, and evidence
Add words to every response

questions.question: A question asks for an inference. What should the student do?
choices: Select a statement copied word for word only
Choose a personal belief with no text support
Ignore the passage
Combine clues from the text with reasonable background understanding

questions.question: What is the best response to a confusing test direction?
choices: Reread it carefully and ask the proctor if clarification is allowed
Assume a different instruction
Skip the entire test
Ask another student for answers

questions.question: A student notices anxiety increasing during a test. Which action is useful and appropriate?
choices: Rush through the remaining questions
Pause briefly, breathe slowly, and return attention to the next task
Stop reading
Change answers without checking

questions.question: Why should students show work on a math response when requested?
choices: It guarantees full credit regardless of accuracy
It replaces the final answer
It makes reasoning visible and can help locate an error
It makes the question shorter

questions.question: An answer choice contains an absolute word such as 'always.' What should a student do?
choices: Reject it automatically
Choose it because it sounds certain
Ignore the word
Check whether the evidence truly supports such a broad statement

questions.question: Which practice best supports time management?
choices: Check time at planned intervals and adjust pace without abandoning careful reading
Spend equal time on every word
Watch the clock continuously
Use all time on the first question

questions.question: A student is asked to cite text evidence. What should the response include?
choices: A page number with no detail
A relevant detail and an explanation of how it supports the answer
A personal reaction only
A quotation unrelated to the claim

questions.question: A test asks for the central idea of a passage. Which answer is strongest?
choices: A minor example
A detail from the title only
A statement that captures the passage's main point rather than one detail
A personal opinion about the topic

questions.question: After completing a test, a student finds a skipped item. What should the student do?
choices: Leave it blank by habit
Copy a nearby answer
Change an unrelated response
Answer it if time and test rules permit, then check the response
